messages:
anya: Quick question — choosing a validation pattern for the new multi-step workspace form. Leaning toward inline errors on blur + a top summary on submit. Also: required fields — asterisk only, or asterisk + visible "(required)"? Screenshot: https://screenshot.internal/xyz 
caleb: From PM pov: inline gives faster feedback. Summary is fine for 10+ fields. For destructive actions I want a typed confirmation for anything that drops data.
tess: Agree with inline. Implementation note: make sure we use aria-invalid + role="alert" on error nodes. Summary is okay but needs focus management so screen readers catch it.
raj: A11y: asterisk alone is ambiguous. Use a visually-hidden "required" label for screen readers. If we go summary-on-submit, move focus to the summary and announce the number of errors.
mika: Eng: perf is fine. For the batch-create flow I vote summary + inline hints; for simpler flows, inline-only. Proposed behavior: show inline on blur, and if submit fails show a condensed summary at top with anchor links.
anya: Quick poll: 1) Inline-on-blur + summary-on-submit? 2) Asterisk + visually-hidden 'required'? 3) Destructive confirmation: typed name for critical, simple modal for minor deletes. Thumbs up for 1/2/3?
caleb: :+1: for all. Copy note: prefer 'Enter a value' over 'This field is required' where we can be more helpful.
tess: Copy nit: use sentence case. Example: 'Please enter your workspace name.' For critical deletes: "Type the workspace name to confirm deletion." Short and explicit.
raj: Accessibility nit for typed confirm: ensure input has aria-label and aria-describedby that points to the consequences text. Also trap focus and provide a cancel shortcut.
anya: Ok I'll update the pattern doc and the component spec with examples and code snippets. Plan: 
- Inline errors: show on blur, aria-invalid + role=alert
- Summary: show on submit if >1 error, focus to summary
- Required marker: asterisk + visually-hidden 'required' text
- Destructive: typed confirm for destructive operations that are irreversible
Anyone object?
caleb: No objections.
tess: No objections. I'll add the focus-handling helper to the component.
raj: No objections.
mika: No objections. Will add tests for keyboard flows.
design-bot: Link updated: https://redwood/design/docs/validation-patterns — spec updated (anya)
anya: Thanks all :heart:
